# Skill Creator authoring boundary

This directory owns portable Skill instructions, current scenario data and retained
historical references. Root instructions apply; task-specific restrictions prevail.

- `references/assessment-guide.md` owns dated prompt/context/authoring knowledge
  and the 41-rule assessment checklist. Apply it at create design/final, actual-source
  audit and evidence-led improve/final; wire consuming links, not orphan references.
  Functional Markdown/XML is authoring policy, not schema validity or measured gain.
- Use recorded Agent Skills format sources; refresh upstream before changing a
  public format contract. Evaluation suite metadata is not Agent Skills frontmatter.
- Keep metadata and instructions English, concise descriptions third-person, and
  SKILL.md <=500 lines. Link conditional detail at its consuming action.
- Author standalone Skills in the user-approved workspace, not a live installation.
  Agent, hook, plugin and executable-packaging responsibilities remain separate.
  Comparative evaluation accepts both Skill and Plugin roots; this does not grant
  whole-plugin authoring authority.
- Current executable source is apps/agent-plugin. Never hand-edit runtime/ or the
  generated scripts/skill-creator.mjs launcher. Report helpers/templates have their
  own ownership; instructions-only changes do not require runtime regeneration.
- Current commands/options are documented in references/command-contract.md;
  README.md links to it and references/evaluate-workflow.md governs orchestration.
  Retired creator commands, receipts, schemas and fixtures are historical only.
- evals/evals.json uses only current executable fields. Freeze assertions outside
  natural user prompts; verify preparation outside the suite, not unsupported
  suite constraints. Supply identical neutral task inputs to both comparison arms.
- Preserve current normative sources, authentic evidence and user changes; obsolete synthetic fixture corpora are not mandatory retention. Never package secrets or
  mutate ~/.agents. A private HOME is not an OS sandbox.
- For instruction changes, inspect local links, containment, suite input existence,
  unsupported fields and line counts. The contained launcher can perform read-only
  `validate <canonical-skill-path>` and evaluation `--dry-run`; neither proves behavior.
  Follow root/app verification guidance for source implementation changes.
- Report actual checks and remaining proof gaps. No implicit models, grading,
  installation, credentials, Git, tracking or publication authority follows from this file.

## Host version policy

Active instructions target current stable host releases and current official documentation.
Do not teach historical version branches unless the user explicitly requests an older target.
Record agent-plugin version, host/version, feature, evidence and verification status in
compatibility matrices instead. A documented capability is not a tested integration;
unsupported or untested hosts remain explicitly unverified. Refresh upstream before
changing public contracts and keep exact runtime versions in execution provenance.

## Host changes, compatibility matrix and changelog

When a host update (Goose, Claude or another supported agent host) is identified as
changing plugin specifications or behavior, inspect its official changelog/release
notes and the affected documentation or implementation before changing the contract.
Record the host version transition, affected feature/specification, concrete impact
and required adaptation in the compatibility matrix, linked from the corresponding
plugin changelog entry. Include agent-plugin version/source revision, exact host
versions, dated upstream sources, verification evidence and status (documented,
tested, unsupported or unverified). Record no relevant impact only when inspected
evidence supports that conclusion; a version bump alone is not a compatibility result.

Maintain the matrix and plugin changelog together for the authorized change. Preserve
historical rows and prior evidence; do not replace an observed version with a vague
"latest" label. A host changelog claim is documented evidence, not a passed integration
test. Keep ordinary Skill instructions on the current supported behavior rather than
adding historical branches. If no plugin changelog/location exists, report that gap
and confirm its destination before creating one; never invent an entry or imply a
release occurred. Missing verification stays explicit and is tracked in Beads.

This maintenance obligation authorizes neither automatic installation/upgrades nor
credentials, model execution, commits, pushes or publication. Apply current task
scope and action-specific authorization before any such operation.

### Compatibility range per agent-plugin version

For each agent-plugin release, state the declared supported host range separately
from exact observed versions, for example `Goose >=1.40.0` (illustrative only, not
an established minimum). A range is a support commitment; derive its lower bound
from the required capabilities and inspected host evidence, record its rationale,
exceptions/upper bound when applicable, and verify the boundary before labeling
it tested. Do not infer `>=` compatibility from one successful newer version.
Keep exact tested host versions and results in separate evidence columns; identify
untested versions within a declared range explicitly. A later host regression must
update the range/limitations and linked plugin changelog rather than silently
retaining an unlimited `+` claim. Unknown lower bounds remain unverified, not guessed.
# Skill Creator executable seams — agent instructions and code map

## Mandatory rule: review documentation impact with every code change

For every code modification, assess whether applicable `AGENTS.md` files still
accurately describe entrypoints, options, contracts, call order and safety boundaries.
Read ancestor instructions and relevant source before editing; automatically update
owned affected maps in the same change. If a map is outside authorized ownership,
report the required correction instead of silently expanding scope. When no update
is needed, give the reason in the handoff, not a no-change log in this file.

This is an agent instruction, not a hook or CI enforcement mechanism. Its directory
scope is `skills/skill-creator/scripts/`; ancestor rules remain applicable. Paths
below are relative to this file. Static documentation checks do not prove runtime
behavior or agent compliance.

## Current entrypoints and ownership

This Skill contains exactly three scripts: the generated CLI launcher, the
source-owned report helper and the source-owned multi-campaign dashboard helper
(`generate-dashboard.mjs`). All require Node.js >=22.22.2. End users need the
whole contained Skill, not Python, an upstream checkout, root tooling or npm setup.

```text
skill-creator.mjs
  -> ../runtime/runtime-manifest.json
  -> spawn(Node, ../runtime/dist/index.js, arguments)
     -> main() -> createApplication() -> createCli() -> selected command handler

generate-report.mjs
  -> verifiedExport(explicit export root)
  -> managedLocation() + managedInventory() when using the managed default
  -> shared .agent-plugin-report.lock -> reverify export
  -> renderReport() -> buildReportData()
```

## Launcher execution and integrity boundary

The launcher validates Node version, its own plain-file path, manifest identity and
mapping, every inventoried runtime file's size/hash, and the exact runtime tree.
`plain()` rejects symlink path segments; `canonical()` rejects unsafe relative
inventory paths. Unlisted files/directories are rejected before runtime import.

It spawns the same Node executable with explicit arguments and inherited streams,
clearing `NODE_PATH` and `NODE_OPTIONS`. SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP are forwarded to the
child; child close propagates exit status or signal. Failures emit a diagnostic and
nonzero status. This is local integrity checking, not an OS sandbox or authenticated
publisher provenance. Caller-owned streams remain open.

## Current CLI navigation

`main(argv, output)` assembles the CLI and calls `parseAsync(..., {from: "user"})`.
Commander help/parse errors return their exit code; domain errors emit their message,
and unexpected errors emit the generic diagnostic. Command behavior belongs in
`adapters/inbound/cli/handle-*-command.ts` and application use cases, not assembly.

Supported commands are `evaluation`, `activation`, `history`, `inspect`, `grading`, `regrading`,
`judgments`, `export` and standalone Skill-format `validate`. See the
[current command contract](../references/command-contract.md#command-contract) and
[evaluation-to-report workflow](../references/evaluate-workflow.md) for exact
arguments and execution authority. Grading/evaluation/activation can call models; history,
inspect and judgments are read-only. Export reads evidence/grades without mutation
and publishes derived outputs. Report
creation is a separate script, not a CLI `render-report` or `review` command.

### Defaults and storage navigation

Use the tool’s default values. Apply overrides only when explicitly requested by the user. Ask for required values that have no default.

Evaluation: Goose, configured model (no `--model`),
repetitions 3, parallelism 3, 50 turns, timeout 0, heartbeat enabled.
Grading/regrading: Goose, configured model, 20 turns, 600 seconds, heartbeat enabled.
Do not infer overrides from cwd/session provider or select `.artifacts` for durable
data. Required selectors/IDs and requested dry-run governance remain applicable.

[evaluation-locations.ts](../../../apps/agent-plugin/src/adapters/outbound/storage/evaluation-locations.ts)
resolves the shared XDG registry and sibling campaigns root on execution. Omit
evaluation `--registry`/`--output` by default.
[campaign-layout.ts](../../../apps/agent-plugin/src/adapters/outbound/storage/campaign-layout.ts)
provides `publishCampaignDirectory()`: all new CLI campaigns use
`profile=<id>/model=configured-<digest>/campaign=<uuid>` and descriptive
`campaign.json`; explicit output changes only the root. Direct/nested stores remain
flat UUID children. Model keys represent frozen configured host/provider/model identities, not actual backend proof.
Legacy default/requested partitions remain retained, never migrated. The stored DB path and
frozen plan remain resume/history authority; no retained paths are migrated.
Reuse a known nondefault registry for retained access, not a new discretionary
override. Resume accepts only registry, explicitly requested retry-uncertain and
quiet presentation alongside its ID, never new selectors or execution/output flags.
Export and helper `--output` are optional; helper `--workspace` remains required.
[export-campaign.ts](../../../apps/agent-plugin/src/application/use-cases/export-campaign.ts)
obtains validated campaign context through the overview history boundary, not cwd
or a reconstructed Hive path.
[managed-campaign-report.ts](../../../apps/agent-plugin/src/adapters/outbound/reporting/managed-campaign-report.ts)
owns `publishManagedCampaignReport()`: default `<recorded-campaign>/report/export`,
private ownership marker, exact inventory authentication and shared report lock.
Explicit destinations remain new/exclusive and outside protected roots. Use default
export/report locations without a destination question. Candidate preparation still
requires a destination with no default.

## Report helper contract and navigation

```bash
node <skill-root>/scripts/generate-report.mjs --help
node <skill-root>/scripts/generate-report.mjs --workspace /path/to/export-root
# Only when an output override is explicitly requested:
node <skill-root>/scripts/generate-report.mjs --workspace /path/to/export-root --output /existing/parent/NEW-review.html
```

Resolve `<skill-root>` to the loaded Skill independently of cwd. The parser requires
unique `--workspace` and accepts optional unique `--output`/`--skill-name`. Workspace
means the export root containing `export-manifest.json`, not `iteration-1`, SQLite
or an evidence archive. Omitted output uses authenticated managed
`<campaign>/report/review.html` when the manifest binds `reportLocation`; an external/legacy
export without that binding defaults to exclusive sibling `review.html`. Explicit
